client: Hi Luna, I've been really struggling with family gatherings lately. Ever since my grandmother passed away last month, I just can't seem to enjoy them. All I can think about is how much I miss her and how empty it feels without her there. I know it's been tough, but I'm not sure if talking about it will really help.
therapist: Hi there, I can hear how deeply you're feeling the absence of your grandmother, and it's completely understandable that family gatherings might feel different and harder without her. It’s okay to take your time with these feelings, and talking about it can be a way to process and honor her memory, even if it feels challenging right now.
vocal_descriptors: very high pitch, very quiet, moderate-paced speech

therapist: I can hear the depth of your emotions and the pressure you feel to keep up with everyone else. It’s completely understandable to feel stuck and worried about making things awkward. Maybe we can think about ways to share your feelings in a way that feels manageable for you, so you don’t have to carry this burden alone.
